items.q: Which three findings together are cardinal signs of leprosy?
o: Butterfly rash, oral ulcers, positive ANA
Anaesthetic skin patch, thickened peripheral nerve, positive slit-skin smear
Itchy vesicles, eosinophilia, positive patch test
items.exp: The cardinal signs are a hypopigmented anaesthetic patch, enlarged peripheral nerve with dysfunction, and demonstrable bacilli on smear.
r: Incorrect. Those suggest vascular disease.
Incorrect. Those suggest lupus.
Correct. All three are cardinal signs.
Incorrect. Those suggest allergy, not leprosy.
items.kp: Numb patch plus thick nerve plus smear is leprosy.

items.q: A patient has a single well-defined dry hairless plaque with a raised edge and complete loss of sweating. The Ridley-Jopling type is?
items.exp: Tuberculoid disease shows few sharply defined anaesthetic hairless lesions with strong cell-mediated immunity and negative smears.
r: Incorrect. That has keloid-like nodules in relapse.
Correct. Single dry hairless numb plaque.
Incorrect. That has numerous symmetric shiny lesions.
Incorrect. That has many lesions with smear positivity.
items.kp: One dry numb plaque is tuberculoid.

items.q: A patient has symmetrical shiny nodules on the face and ears with eyebrow loss and nasal congestion. The expected smear result is?
items.exp: Lepromatous leprosy has heavy bacillary loads with foamy macrophages and globi on smears from skin and earlobes.
r: Correct. Multibacillary with globi.
Incorrect. Negativity marks tuberculoid disease.
Incorrect. Skin smears are strongly positive.
Incorrect. Smears stay positive throughout.
items.kp: Many shiny nodules mean strongly positive smear.

items.q: During treatment a borderline patient develops sudden swelling, redness and scaling of old patches with painful neuritis. This type 1 reaction is?
o: Immune-complex deposition with fever and nodules
Drug allergy needing immediate multidrug stoppage
Upgrading cell-mediated inflammation needing urgent nerve protection
items.exp: Type 1 reversal reactions are delayed-hypersensitivity flares in borderline disease threatening nerves, managed with anti-inflammatory cover.
r: Incorrect. That describes type 2 erythema nodosum.
Incorrect. Allergy has different timing and signs.
Incorrect. Relapse grows new lesions, not inflamed old ones.
Correct. Reversal neuritis threatens nerve function.
items.kp: Swollen old patches with neuritis is reversal.

items.q: A lepromatous patient develops crops of painful red nodules with fever, joint pains and eye redness. This type 2 reaction shows?
items.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum is an immune-complex reaction with tender nodules, fever, arthritis, iridocyclitis and orchitis.
r: Incorrect. Macules alone do not define ENL.
Incorrect. Nodes alone do not define ENL.
Correct. Tender nodules with systemic inflammation.
Incorrect. Neuritis dominates type 1, not type 2.
items.kp: Painful nodule crops with fever is ENL.

items.q: Slit-skin smears in leprosy are best taken from earlobes and lesion edges because?
o: These cool sites carry the highest bacillary load
These sites never bleed during slitting
Nerves are absent at these sites
items.exp: Mycobacterium leprae prefers cooler skin so earlobes, eyebrows and active edges give the best yields for bacterial and morphologic indices.
r: Incorrect. Healing speed is not the reason.
Correct. Cool sites concentrate bacilli.
Incorrect. Bleeding occurs at any slit site.
Incorrect. Nerve sampling is separate.
items.kp: Cool earlobes give the best smears.

items.q: Under the Indian NLEP, leprosy treatment follows the multidrug principle chiefly to?
o: Prevent drug resistance with combination therapy
Shorten therapy to a single dose for all
Replace clinical follow-up with drugs alone
items.exp: The programme uses multidrug combinations to cure infection, prevent resistance and shorten infectivity, with reaction care alongside.
r: Correct. Combinations prevent resistance.
Incorrect. Duration depends on classification.
Incorrect. Follow-up for nerves and reactions continues.
Incorrect. Antimicrobials treat the infection itself.

items.q: A treated leprosy patient cannot close the eye fully and has a drooping mouth angle. The nerve most likely damaged is?
items.exp: Facial involvement causes lagophthalmos with corneal risk and lower-face weakness; ulnar gives claw hand and peroneal gives foot drop.
r: Incorrect. Ulnar affects the hand.
Incorrect. Peroneal affects foot dorsiflexion.
Incorrect. Tibial affects plantar foot.
Correct. Eye closure and mouth angle are facial.

items.q: A diffuse lepromatous patient develops painful black necrotic patches on the legs with fever. This Lucio phenomenon reflects?
o: Bacillary invasion of vessel walls with ischaemic necrosis
items.exp: Lucio phenomenon is necrotising vasculopathy of diffuse lepromatous disease from endothelial bacillary load and thrombosis.
r: Incorrect. Stasis ulcers sit above malleoli.
Incorrect. Emboli give single-territory infarcts.
Correct. Vessel-wall bacilli infarct skin.
Incorrect. Drug eruptions differ in pattern.
items.kp: Necrotic patches in diffuse leprosy mean Lucio.

items.q: Years after apparent cure, a patient grows shiny keloid-like nodules on normal skin with very high bacillary counts. This is?
items.exp: Histoid leprosy is a relapse form with spindle-cell nodules teeming with bacilli, a reservoir needing retreatment.
r: Incorrect. Lymphoma shows atypical lymphocytes.
Correct. Shiny nodules with teeming bacilli.
Incorrect. Keloids lack bacilli and follow injury.
Incorrect. Dermatofibromas dimple and lack bacilli.
items.kp: Shiny nodules after cure mean histoid relapse.
